title: Evidence & Retry Ladder Playbook for Customers
content:
Purpose:
This working draft is a combined status-page snippet and customer-facing post-incident playbook focused on: (1) providing concise verification artifacts customers can use to confirm impact and (2) a retry/replay ladder that minimizes duplicated work and protects downstream data integrity. 

High-level summary (one-line for status page):
Short window of increased response variance for text-generation in eu-west-1 between 2027-05-26T21:12Z and 2027-05-26T21:49Z; partial mitigation applied at 21:28Z. Root cause: transient KV-cache eviction under an unexpected load pattern; fix: runtime guard to pin hot KV segments. No customer data leaked.

Status page snippet (3 variants):
- Minimal (statuspage headline): "Investigating: brief service variance for text generation in eu-west-1 — possible higher latency and anomalous outputs for a subset of requests."
- Recommended (public customers): "We observed a short disruption in generation quality and latency in eu-west-1 on 2027-05-26. We rolled a partial mitigation at 21:28Z; full remediation completed at 21:49Z. Affected requests may see duplicated or truncated tokens; we are providing replay artifacts and verification steps below."
- Partner/enterprise (data + timeline): "Between 2027-05-26T21:12Z–21:49Z, ~0.7% of generation requests in eu-west-1 experienced KV-cache misalignment leading to malformed or truncated outputs. We deployed a conservative KV pinning guard at 21:28Z which reduced incidents immediately; final rollback and configuration hardening completed by 21:49Z. See evidence package for request IDs and checksums."

Customer-facing postmortem summary (executive paragraph):
What happened: A memory allocation pattern under a specific burst pattern caused the runtime to evict hot KV entries prematurely, which in some cases produced unexpected token truncation or duplicated tokens during streaming responses. Impact: Approximately 0.7% of generation requests in eu-west-1 between 21:12Z and 21:49Z. Why now: New traffic shape from a high-concurrency customer test that mixed short-sequence and long-sequence streams.

Timeline (customer-facing, concise):
- 21:12Z — First elevated anomaly alerts (error rate on generation checksum).
- 21:18Z — Operators identify KV-cache churn signal correlated with high-concurrency pattern.
- 21:28Z — Deployed KV pinning guard (partial mitigation). Customer-impact reduced but not fully eliminated.
- 21:49Z — Full remediation via config hardening and rollback of an aggressive eviction optimization.
- 22:15Z — Additional verification sweep completed; no further anomalies observed.

What we did (actions taken and why):
- Immediate mitigation: rolled a guard to prevent eviction of the most recently accessed KV segments for 2 minutes to stabilize streams.
- Root-cause fix: reverted an aggressive eviction heuristic introduced in PR #1842 and implemented a safe fallback in runtime that prefers pinning when mixed sequence distributions are detected.
- Post-incident operational: added a real-time detection rule for KV churn and an automated canary that simulates short/long sequence mixes before aggressive eviction heuristics are enabled.

Evidence package for customers (what we provide):
- List of affected request IDs (sampled) with UTC timestamps, model, and tenant-id (where permitted).
- Response checksums (SHA256) of pre/post replay outputs for a small sample set.
- Operator proof: trace IDs for requests that hit the eviction path (span:eviction-check).
- Simple verifier script (Python) to fetch request body, replay locally against the provided model snapshot, and compare checksums. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/IN-4218#evidence

Customer verification steps (recommended order):
1) Identify your tenant request IDs from logs around 2027-05-26T21:10–21:50Z.
2) Use our verifier script (requires API key with replay scope) to fetch stored request payloads and run against the supplied model snapshot.
3) Confirm checksums and token sequences; if mismatch persists, open a ticket with the packaged evidence (request IDs + trace IDs).

Retry / Replay ladder (to minimize duplicated side effects):
- Tier 0 (safe, idempotent): Re-run read-only generation calls with the same prompt and model version. Safe for stateless prompts.
- Tier 1 (with state): For cases where your app attaches dedup keys or idempotency keys, use our replay endpoint with the same idempotency token — this will only re-run if the original request was not marked completed.
- Tier 2 (non-idempotent): If your workflow triggers downstream side effects (e.g., database writes), reach out to customer success before replay — we will coordinate a curated replay to avoid duplication and provide a safe window.

Compensation and SLA considerations (customer-facing):
- We are tracking SLA credit eligibility for tenants with requests impacted in this window. If your usage met your committed throughput and you experienced errors or malformed outputs, CS will surface a tailored credit proposal.

Customer action checklist (short):
- Run verifier on a representative sample (recommended 50–200 requests).
- Escalate if any critical production traffic is affected (open ticket with request IDs).
- Consider toggling to a pinned-model routing for short-term stability if you operate heavy mixed-sequence traffic.

Internal notes / TODOs (do not publish as-is):
- [ ] Finalize list of affected request IDs across enterprise tenants (privacy review required).
- [ ] Prepare e-mail template for impacted partners with evidence bundle attached.
- [ ] Confirm SLA credit thresholds and recipient list with finance.
- [ ] Add snippet to statuspage (approved language) once legal blesses the wording above.

Open questions for engineering/product:
- Do we want automatic tenant-level pinning when a tenant exceeds 80% mixed-sequence traffic for 1 minute? (ops suggestion: yes, soft-limit)
notes_short: Working draft: statuspage + customer verification + replay ladder. For CS review and legal sign-off before publishing.
